title: New Alzheimer’s Trial Begins Testing Drug on People Without Symptoms
subtitle: Researchers are launching a major international study to see if a new medicine can prevent dementia before it starts.

summary.en: A new international medical trial called PrevenTRON has officially started testing an experimental drug on healthy individuals. The study focuses on people aged 55 to 80 who show no current signs of memory loss but are at higher risk for Alzheimer’s disease. Researchers are using a specific blood test to identify a protein linked to future cognitive decline. If successful, this drug could stop the disease before it ever develops. The trial is expected to last several years as experts monitor the long-term effects on participants.
summary.zh: 一項名為 PrevenTRON 的國際醫學新試驗已正式開始對健康個體進行實驗性藥物測試。該研究聚焦於五十五至八十歲、目前無記憶喪失跡象但罹患阿茲海默症風險較高的人群。研究人員正利用特定的血液檢測來識別與未來認知能力衰退相關的蛋白質。若試驗成功，此藥物可能在疾病發展前就將其阻斷。由於專家需監測參與者的長期影響，預計該試驗將持續數年。

paragraphs.en: A major new medical study is now underway, marking a significant change in how doctors approach Alzheimer’s disease. As reported by The Guardian Health, the PrevenTRON trial has begun screening its first European participants. This international research project aims to discover if an experimental drug can stop dementia before any symptoms appear in patients.
paragraphs.zh: 一項重大的醫學新研究現正展開，標誌著醫師處理阿茲海默症（Alzheimer’s disease）的方式出現了重大轉變。根據《衛報健康版》（The Guardian Health）報導，PrevenTRON 試驗已開始篩選首批歐洲參與者。這項國際研究計畫旨在探索一種實驗性藥物是否能在患者出現任何症狀前，就先阻斷失智症的發展。

paragraphs.en: For many years, medical research focused on treating Alzheimer’s only after patients began to lose their memory or experience other signs of cognitive decline. However, experts are now shifting their focus toward prevention. Prof Ramin Nilforooshan, the chief investigator for the trial, explained that the goal is to act much earlier. He noted that the team wants to see if they can stop the disease before symptoms even begin. By targeting the condition at an early stage, researchers hope to help millions of people who might otherwise develop the disease later in life.
paragraphs.zh: 多年來，醫學研究僅專注於患者開始喪失記憶或出現其他認知能力衰退跡象後的治療。然而，專家們現在正將重心轉向預防。該試驗的首席研究員尼爾福魯山教授（Prof Ramin Nilforooshan）解釋，目標是要更早採取行動。他指出，研究團隊希望觀察是否能在疾病症狀出現前就將其遏止。透過在早期階段針對病況進行干預，研究人員希望能幫助數百萬名未來可能罹患此病的人。

paragraphs.en: The trial is recruiting approximately 1,600 people between the ages of 55 and 80 from around the world. To be eligible, participants must be healthy and show no current memory problems. The process begins with a blood test to check for a specific biomarker called p-tau217. A biomarker is a substance in the body that can be measured to show the presence or progress of a disease. Previous research indicates that high levels of p-tau217 can predict cognitive decline with high accuracy. According to The Guardian Health, people with the highest levels of this protein have an estimated 78% chance of developing memory issues within 10 years.
paragraphs.zh: 這項試驗正從全球招募約一千六百名年齡介於五十五至八十歲的人士。參與者必須身體健康且目前沒有記憶問題才符合資格。篩選過程始於一項血液檢測，用以檢查一種稱為 p-tau217 的特定生物標記。生物標記是指體內可被測量以顯示疾病存在或進展的物質。先前的研究顯示，高濃度的 p-tau217 能以極高準確度預測認知能力衰退。根據《衛報健康版》，體內含有最高濃度此類蛋白質的人，在十年內出現記憶問題的機率估計高達百分之七十八。

paragraphs.en: The drug being tested is called trontinemab, developed by the Swiss pharmaceutical company Roche. It works by attacking amyloid plaques, which are toxic proteins that build up in the brain and eventually kill brain cells. Early tests showed that the drug successfully cleared these plaques in nine out of 10 people who were already in the early stages of Alzheimer’s. Because of these promising results, scientists are now testing if the drug can provide similar benefits to people who have not yet developed any symptoms at all.
paragraphs.zh: 受測藥物名為 trontinemab，由瑞士藥廠羅氏（Roche）開發。其作用機制是攻擊類澱粉蛋白斑塊，這是一種會在腦部堆積並最終殺死腦細胞的毒性蛋白質。早期測試顯示，該藥物成功清除了十名已處於阿茲海默症早期階段患者中九人的斑塊。由於這些令人振奮的結果，科學家們現在正測試該藥物是否能為尚未出現任何症狀的人提供類似的益處。

paragraphs.en: While the potential for this treatment is exciting, researchers are careful to manage expectations. Prof Nilforooshan emphasized that the drug is still experimental. In an interview with the Telegraph, he explained that the team must wait to see if the treatment truly works. He stated that the trial is not a magic solution, but rather a scientific investigation to gather more data. The study is designed to last between four and six years. During this time, participants will be randomly assigned to receive either the drug or a placebo, which is a substance with no active medicine, used to compare results fairly.
paragraphs.zh: 雖然這種治療方法的潛力令人振奮，但研究人員謹慎地管理大眾的期望。尼爾福魯山教授強調，該藥物仍處於實驗階段。他在接受《每日電訊報》（The Telegraph）採訪時解釋，團隊必須等待觀察治療是否真的有效。他表示，這項試驗並非神奇的解決方案，而是一項為了收集更多數據的科學調查。該研究預計持續四到六年。在此期間，參與者將被隨機分配接受藥物或安慰劑，後者是一種不含活性藥物的物質，用於公平地比較結果。

paragraphs.en: The Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS foundation trust is leading the recruitment process in the UK. At least 15 hospitals and clinics are expected to participate in the study by the end of the year. This effort is part of a larger, global mission to understand if Alzheimer’s can be stopped before it changes a person’s life. Alzheimer’s disease is a serious condition that affects roughly one in 14 people over the age of 65, and the risk increases significantly as people get older. Because the disease is thought to develop inside the brain up to 10 years before symptoms typically appear, this trial represents a critical opportunity to intervene while the brain is still healthy.
paragraphs.zh: 英國的薩里與邊界夥伴國民保健署信託基金會（Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS foundation trust）正主導英國境內的招募程序。預計到今年年底，將有至少十五家醫院與診所參與這項研究。這項努力是全球性任務的一部分，旨在了解是否能在阿茲海默症改變一個人的人生之前將其阻止。阿茲海默症是一種嚴重的疾病，約影響十四分之一的六十五歲以上人口，且風險會隨著年齡增長而顯著增加。由於該疾病被認為在症狀通常出現前十年就已在腦內發展，這項試驗代表了一個在腦部仍健康時進行干預的關鍵機會。

paragraphs.en: For those interested in the study, the research team is currently accepting inquiries. As the trial continues, the medical community will be watching closely to see if this new approach can change the future of dementia care. If trontinemab proves effective, it could offer a new way to protect brain health for older adults worldwide. For now, the focus remains on careful monitoring and gathering evidence to determine if this new strategy is safe and successful.
paragraphs.zh: 對於對此研究感興趣的人士，研究團隊目前正接受諮詢。隨著試驗持續進行，醫學界將密切關注這種新方法是否能改變失智症照護的未來。如果 trontinemab 被證實有效，它可能為全球老年人提供一種保護腦部健康的新途徑。目前，重點仍放在謹慎監測並收集證據，以確定這項新策略是否安全且成功。

quiz.question: What is the primary requirement for individuals to be considered eligible for the PrevenTRON trial?

options.A: They must be at least 65 years old and show early signs of memory loss.
options.B: They must be between 55 and 80 years old and currently show no memory problems.
options.C: They must have already been diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease by a hospital.
options.D: They must have high levels of p-tau217 and be currently receiving treatment for dementia.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，試驗招募的對象為 55 到 80 歲且「健康且無記憶問題」的人。選項 A 錯誤，因為試驗要求無記憶問題；選項 C 錯誤，因為試驗目標是預防症狀出現，而非治療已確診患者；選項 D 錯誤，雖提到 p-tau217，但試驗是為了透過檢測該指標來篩選參與者，而非要求參與者必須已經確診。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why are researchers focusing on the period 10 years before symptoms appear?

options.A: Because that is when the drug trontinemab is most affordable to produce.
options.B: Because they believe the disease has already started to develop in the brain by that time.
options.C: Because the p-tau217 biomarker only exists in the body for a decade.
options.D: Because they want to ensure participants have enough time to finish the 4-6 year study.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第六段，該疾病被認為在症狀出現前 10 年就已在腦中發展，因此研究人員認為此時是介入治療的關鍵時機。選項 A 文章未提及藥物成本；選項 C 錯誤，文章並未說該指標只存在十年；選項 D 雖然提到研究長度，但這並非研究選擇該時間點進行介入的邏輯原因。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the word 'manage' mean in the phrase 'manage expectations'?

options.A: To increase the public's excitement about a new medical discovery.
options.B: To control or limit the amount of information given to the public.
options.C: To keep hopes realistic and prevent people from assuming the trial is a guaranteed cure.
options.D: To organize the daily schedules of the patients participating in the trial.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。在文中 'manage expectations' 指的是保持理性與務實的態度，避免大眾過度樂觀。選項 A 與文意相反，研究人員強調這不是「魔法解決方案」；選項 B 錯誤，這不是關於隱瞞資訊；選項 D 錯誤，這與管理病患行程無關。此用法在學術與醫學溝通中常見，意指調整大眾對結果的預期。

quiz.question: What is the central message of this article regarding the PrevenTRON trial?

options.A: The trial has already proven that trontinemab can successfully cure Alzheimer’s disease.
options.B: Doctors are shifting their focus from treating Alzheimer’s symptoms to preventing the disease before it starts.
options.C: The Swiss company Roche is the only organization currently researching Alzheimer’s prevention.
options.D: The trial is primarily designed to test the safety of blood tests for older patients.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。本文主旨強調醫學界正將重點從「症狀出現後的治療」轉向「症狀出現前的預防」，並介紹了 PrevenTRON 試驗作為此轉變的代表。選項 A 錯誤，文章強調這仍是實驗性質，尚未證實有效；選項 C 錯誤，文章未稱 Roche 是唯一研究機構；選項 D 錯誤，血液檢測僅是篩選手段，而非研究的主要目的。
